messages:
maria: Customer escalated (acct: BrightCart) — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~600ms to ~2s this morning, p95 also up but less dramatic. They say no traffic change on their side. ticket: #4521. I gathered a curl repro and their request id: req-33a9. Can oncall look?
aj: looking. can you paste the exact request headers + example payload? also which model + region?
maria: model=redwood-13b-v2, region=us-west-2, content-type=application/json. payload is ~1.8k tokens (mostly prompt). curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"<redacted prompt>","max_tokens":256}'```

maria: customer attached a screenshot of our dashboard p99 panel (shows 2s) and Grafana histogram raw query (shows many ops still <1s but a long tail). they think our dashboard is lying.
tom: pinging metrics. which dashboard/panel is that? is it the per-route quantile rollup or the raw request histogram? those differ depending on rollup window and bucketization.
leah: I pulled the panels. The 'API /v1/generate latency p99 (route-level)' panel is a quantile over rollup-aggregated series (60s rollup, 5m retention), while the histogram panel uses raw samples from the ingest pipeline and does a percentile client-side. So differences expected if long tail is sparse.
leah: quick check: over the last hour raw samples p99=1.9s, but when we downsample and do 60s rollup we get 2.05s. not huge but visible. I also see a spike of a small number (~120) of requests with 4-6s latency between 08:12-08:18 UTC. those are the tail.
aj: are those coming from a single customer or many? trace ids? can we correlate to req-33a9?
leah: correlating... most 4-6s traces map to nodepool-3 instances in us-west-2. A few have high queue_time and large decoder steps. attaching trace ids: trace-9a4, trace-9b2, trace-9d1.
tom: nodepool-3 had a rolling kernel update yesterday at 02:00 and auto-restart of some pods. I see a small % of pods with an older runtime (nvtx-kernel 1.7) where a batching bug increases latency for long prompts. getting logs now.
maria: customer says they didn't change prompt size. they repro'd at 08:15 with same payload and saw p99=2.1s. So likely infra.
leah: query I ran (pseudo): ```SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) FROM request_samples WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND region='us-west-2' GROUP BY 1m``` gives the spike bucket. Rollup config: 60s sample_window, method=approx_quantile. That explains slight differences vs histogram.
aj: mitigation options? can we route this customer's traffic off nodepool-3 or apply a temporary model fallback?
tom: two quick mitigations: 1) exclude nodepool-3 from routing for new requests (weight 0) until we patch runtime (low risk), or 2) set a per-cust routing policy to route BrightCart to nodepool-1 (we can do a quick override). Also we can enable the older batching logic for nodepool-3.
maria: customer wants immediate fix, can we do option 2 now? their SLA is impacted.
tom: assigning to aj to execute override. i'll push a hotfix to the runtime later today.
aj: doing per-cust override now: ```rbctl route override --customer BrightCart --route /v1/generate --target nodepool-1 --ttl 2h``` applying... :eyes: deploy-bot: "route-override applied by aj for BrightCart -> nodepool-1 (ttl=2h)"
aj: done. can BrightCart confirm? maria: pinged them, they're running a quick test.
maria: they confirm p99 dropped to ~700ms after the override. they say thanks but want permanent fix.
leah: follow-ups: 1) telemetry owner to verify rollup vs raw percentile doc is clear in dashboard, 2) add anomaly alerting on small-volume high-latency tails so we don't miss sparse spikes, 3) runtime team to patch batching bug.
tom: I'll schedule a postmortem for the nodepool kernel/batching interaction and label remediation. owner: tom. ETA hotfix by EOD.
aj: noted. For immediate customer-facing comms: maria to send status update and mitigation summary.
maria: I'll send now. draft: "we routed your traffic to an unaffected pool and observed p99 return to expected levels. engineering is patching the node runtime and we'll follow up with a permanent timeline"

leah: one more note for observability: we'll add a small-panel showing sample counts next to quantile panels to reduce interpretation errors — low sample counts + sparse tails caused confusion here.
maria: thanks all. closing loop with customer after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
